question: How is obscuration-destruction in own cause not impermanent, and likewise for taste-to-sound?
premises: in its own cause, obscuration-destruction — that by which not impermanent
inference: Cause-contained cessation is not impermanent; same for every sense-tanmatra.
plain_english: In its own cause, obscuration-destruction — that by which not impermanent; thus in taste-to-sound tanmatras too, connection.
